instructions: Heat the oven to 430°F (220°C) and line 2 large baking sheets with parchment.
Cut the stems off the 2 eggplants and slice them lengthwise about 1/3 inch thick, leaving the skin on.
Brush both sides of the slices with 3 tbsp of the olive oil and lay them on the sheets in a single layer. Sprinkle them with 1/2 tsp of the salt.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, turning the slices and swapping the sheets halfway, until they're golden in patches and soft all the way through when you press one.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion and mince the 3 garlic cloves. Pick the leaves off the basil and keep the stalks.

Heat the last 1 tbsp olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium high. Add the onion and cook for about 3 minutes, stirring, until it's soft and just starting to color at the edges. Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.

Pour in the crushed tomatoes and stir in the 1/2 tsp oregano, 1 tsp sugar and the basil stalks. Bring it to a simmer, then turn the heat down to medium low and simmer uncovered for about 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's thick and a spoonful doesn't run on a plate.
Fish out the basil stalks and stir in the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the 1/4 tsp pepper. Taste the sauce, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat.
When the eggplant is done, take it out and turn the oven down to 350°F (180°C). Finely grate the 4 oz parmesan and shred the 6 oz mozzarella.

Spread 2 big spoonfuls of the sauce over the bottom of an 8 inch square baking dish. Lay a third of the eggplant over it, overlapping a little. Spread a third of the remaining sauce on top, then sprinkle with a third of the parmesan and a small handful of the basil leaves.
Make a second layer the same way, with another third of the eggplant, sauce and parmesan and another small handful of basil.
Finish with the last of the eggplant and sauce, the last of the parmesan and then all the mozzarella.
Bake for 25 minutes, until it's bubbling at the edges and golden on top.
Let it sit for 10 minutes before you cut it, or the layers slide apart. Tear the rest of the basil leaves over the top. Serve with crusty bread and a green salad.
method_notes: Both versions bake the eggplant slices in oil until golden and soft instead of frying them, then layer them with tomato sauce and cheese and bake again until bubbling. RecipeTin Eats leaves the slices unbreaded, makes its own sugo of onion, garlic, passata, canned tomatoes, oregano, a little sugar and basil stalks simmered 30 to 40 minutes, layers in parmesan and basil, and tops only the last layer with mozzarella. Love and Lemons coats the rounds in egg and a panko and parmesan crumb, uses jarred marinara and fresh mozzarella in every layer, and broils the top. This one follows RecipeTin Eats, scaled down to an 8 inch dish for four.
